speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when you first noticed this painful ulcer on your leg and if you have any history of diabetes or poor circulation?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, I suspect this might be an inflammatory condition like pyoderma gangrenosum rather than a simple insect bite reaction. Have you noticed any other skin lesions, joint pain, or changes in your eyes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pitting edema and dilated tortuous veins strongly suggests venous insufficiency, which often complicates leg ulcers. I will order a Doppler ultrasound to assess venous flow and a wound culture to rule out secondary infection. REQUEST TEST: Venous_Doppler

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal venous Doppler effectively rules out venous insufficiency as the primary cause. Given the history of Crohn's disease, the painful nature of the ulcer with purplish borders, and the trauma trigger, I suspect pyoderma gangrenosum. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
